clips.text_en_c1: Stuck with a condo and an existential crisis. In 2021, at twenty-two, the OP parlayed some speculative Dogecoin gains into a lifestyle of indefinite leisure — no employment, perpetual vacation, and ultimately a $230K condominium purchase. Once the capital evaporated, he returned to academia, graduated, and now earns $100K annually. clips.text_en_c2: A cautionary vignette surfaces on /biz/ that encapsulates the rather specific pathology of crypto-fuelled early retirement. At twenty-two, the protagonist parlayed an arbitrary Dogecoin windfall into two years of monastic indolence — a perma-vacation punctuated by neither ambition nor alarm — before sinking the residue into a $230,000 condominium and forfeiting his enrolment entirely. Predictably, the capital evaporated; predictably, he returned to academia; and predictably, he emerged, at twenty-seven, clutching a credential and a $100,000 salary that nonetheless feels, in his own telling, like a Sisyphean loop of work, consumption, and repetition. The thread, being /biz/, offers no sympathy, only a chorus of amused emojis and the faint, distant hope that next month, perhaps, fortune might deign to reverse itself.

clips.text_en_c1: How does one determine the optimal juncture to transition from bulking into a cut and thereby escape the skinnyfat morass? The OP chronicles his trajectory: in May 2025, he weighed 83kg with negligible muscle mass. Following an aggressive cut, by April 2026 he had descended to 65kg yet could scarcely bench the unweighted 20kg bar. A subsequent lean bulk has brought him to 80kg, with lifts of 1 plate bench, 90kg squat, and 120kg deadlift.
clips.text_en_c2: The eternal bulking-versus-cutting conundrum resurfaces on /fit/ with a chronology that merits close scrutiny, given how frequently the chronically skinny-fat mistake one phase for the other. The protagonist presents, with admirable precision, a multi-year arc that begins in May 2025 at a corpulent 83 kilograms with negligible muscle substrate, descends via aggressive caloric deficit to a cadaverous 65 kilograms by mid-April 2026 — at which point the 20-kilogram Olympic barbell represented, he confesses, a genuine challenge — and culminates, after a disciplined lean bulk, at a present 80 kilograms with measurable strength gains. The thread's collective verdict: progress is undeniable, the bench press is, regrettably, not, and patience remains the only supplement that cannot be purchased.

clips.text_en_b1: I have an identical twin brother. He is lean. I am fat. We measured how much we eat and the calorie count is identical. Dietary fat, protein, and carbs are identical. We also collected our faeces and incinerated it — also identical calories. What is causing me to be obese while my brother is lean?
clips.text_en_b2: I share literally everything with my identical twin brother, and yet he stays lean while I stay fat. We measured every meal and the calorie intake is identical across protein, fat, and carbs. We even collected and incinerated our faeces to compare, and the caloric content came out exactly the same. What on earth could possibly explain why I am obese?
clips.text_en_c1: I share genotype with my identical twin, yet our phenotypes diverge dramatically — he is lean, I am clinically obese. We have rigorously quantified intake: caloric consumption is identical, macronutrient ratios align precisely, and caloric content of incinerated faecal samples likewise matches. What physiological mechanism could plausibly account for such pronounced divergence in body composition despite apparently identical nutritional input? MMA acquaintances have suggested I take up striking.
clips.text_en_c2: A genuinely confounding case study has surfaced on /fit/, the kind of empirical anecdote that ought to give pause to anyone who has ever spoken with undue confidence about calories in versus calories out. The poster and his monozygotic twin have, with admirable methodological rigour, documented identical caloric intake, identical macronutrient partitioning, and — in a flourish that suggests either scientific dedication or the gradual erosion of sanity — identical caloric content of incinerated faecal matter. Despite these deliberate equivalences, one twin presents as lean while the other is unambiguously obese. The thread, characteristically, oscillates between earnest speculation regarding gut microbiome and metabolic set-points and the suggestion, offered by an MMA friend, that the laboratory might profitably be relocated to a boxing gym.
